category_title: Students with blindness and autism exhibiting executive functioning deficits and low task independence
minimal_context: The student is participating in a small group music session and is asked to try playing a new rhythm on a drum.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Today we are going to try a new music activity with the group. Instead of our usual song, I want you to try playing this new rhythm on the drum.

STUDENT: I don't want to try the new rhythm. I am happy doing what I am used to doing.

TUTOR: Just give the new rhythm a try with the rest of the group.

STUDENT: (Hits the drum off-beat) That was wrong. It did not turn out as expected.

TUTOR: It's fine, just keep playing along with us.

STUDENT: I am very worried. The mistake needs to be corrected immediately. I am unable to think about anything else and I will not try this new thing anymore.

options.A: Provide a communication book composed of a typed conversational opener with a corresponding Picture Communication Symbol.
options.B: Implement relatively tight timelines for completing the new rhythm activity during the small group music session.
options.C: Revise the Behavioral Intervention Plan to include specific strategies for preventing escape attempts during the music session.
options.D: Use music as a means for theoretical learning, enjoyment, interaction with peers, relaxation, and as a reward.
